ask_text: --issue 140: an unbalanced quote defeats the blanket-staging gate in 59 bytes with no timeout, and the test suite documents the bypass as correct behaviour.

events.note: architectural (mandatory trigger: security domain + hook/gate keywords). 8 reqs/8 ACs, falsifiability clean. Root cause independently verified by orchestrator: the redirection arm at pre-tool-use.sh:1153 marks the heredoc delimiter as a redirect target but never treats the body as an opaque region, so quote-state leaks through. q1 (which shell the Bash tool actually invokes) non-blocking, recorded.

Phase 2 round 1: DBA APPROVE_WITH_NOTES (major: AC1 has no fixture cell for <<- tab-stripped terminators, a genuinely different mechanism than quote parity - independently verified by orchestrator against real bash). DevOps APPROVE_WITH_NOTES (resolved q1: production shell is zsh, confirmed by inspecting its own subprocess; also independently rediscovered the main-branch corpus-drift issue). SecOps REQUEST_CHANGES: core vulnerability confirmed live via two independent oracles with real non-zero controls (26-byte repro, shim-confirmed git invocation), but R1's fixture matrix only crosses one implicit delimiter spelling - SecOps proved <<-EOF and <<'EOF' are ALSO live-exploitable with the identical odd-quote body and are outside AC1's binding matrix, so an implementation could pass every AC while shipping 2 of 3 proven-exploitable spellings. Looping back to BA per the rubric.

Round 2: AC1 widened to 12 cells crossing delimiter-introducer spelling as its own axis; AC9/AC10/AC11 added. 11 ACs, falsifiability clean, contiguous. Orchestrator independently reproduced the <<-EOF composition claim in real bash.

Round 2 closed clean: DBA APPROVE, DevOps and SecOps APPROVE_WITH_NOTES, 0 blocking. SecOps re-verified against literal cell definitions (not the summary), independently caught <<\EOF was untested and verified it live, found AC10 omits a low-risk <<\EOF narrow-stage cell. DevOps independently re-confirmed main is still red on the corpus-drift issue across 3 consecutive runs.

Judge synthesized sketch A (smallest blast radius) as winner, grafting 3 items from sketch B; owner_decision.required=false (sketches converged on mechanism, differed only on reviewability/blast-radius, a technical call). Judge's own empirical check surfaced a genuine, live regression neither Phase-2 round tested: full heredoc-body opacity for an UNQUOTED introducer flips a construction the CURRENT scanner correctly denies today (unquoted <<EOF body containing $(git add -A), via an accidental '(' -driven mechanism) into an allow post-fix, and real zsh/bin-sh genuinely execute that substitution -- a direct violation of spec's own R1 ('mirror a real shell's own treatment') for the unquoted case. Orchestrator routed this to SecOps for a real ruling rather than deciding solo, per the standing instruction to leverage the pipeline for high-risk items. SecOps independently re-reproduced against the actual gate driver AND real zsh/bin-sh (own non-zero control caught first: a non-numeric issue-dir silently produced 'none' for everything including a sanity control), confirmed the finding exactly, ruled it is NOT comparable to the already-accepted #118 verb-opacity gap (this is a fix-introduced regression in the same control the fix is meant to harden, not a pre-existing unrelated gap), and VETOed: closing 4 proven bypasses while opening a comparably-easy 5th in the same commit is not proportionate to ship silently. Specified the minimum spec fix: a narrow additive AC (not a redesign) -- for an UNQUOTED heredoc introducer only, deny outright if the body contains a literal $(, backtick, or ${ before the real terminator; quoted-delimiter bodies stay fully opaque exactly as already specified (confirmed correct against real zsh). SecOps also independently found and reported, as an OUT-OF-SCOPE separate finding, a more severe, currently-untracked, pre-existing bypass: bare backtick substitution (`git add -A`) defeats the gate today with no heredoc at all, because backtick is not in the scanner's structural-character set -- filed as new issue #143, not blocking #140. Full evidence at .pipeline/140/secops-2.5-ruling.json. Looping back to BA for a narrow AC12 addition per SecOps's spec, NOT a full redesign; sketches/design.json stand and are not re-run once the spec is widened, per the standard VETO loop-back.

Round 3 (VETO rework): added AC12 verbatim per SecOps's required_minimum_spec_change -- for an unquoted heredoc introducer, deny outright if the body contains a literal $(, backtick, or ${ before the real terminator; quoted-delimiter bodies stay fully opaque per AC1/R1, unchanged. 4 fixture cells added, all taken verbatim from SecOps's own real-gate-driver-plus-real-zsh reproduction. 12 ACs total, falsifiability-clean, contiguous. R1-R8/AC1-AC11 confirmed byte-identical, q1 not reopened, design.json/sketches untouched (additive-only, no redesign needed).

Round 3 closed clean, scoped confirmation only (not a full re-review of AC1-AC11, already approved twice). DBA APPROVE: confirmed AC12 touches no schema/migration/access-policy surface. DevOps APPROVE: confirmed AC12 is in-process only, no subprocess/network/CI/deploy surface. SecOps VETO LIFTED, APPROVE_WITH_NOTES: AC12 checked field-by-field against SecOps's own required_minimum_spec_change (scope condition, three literal sequences, coarse fail-closed minimum, non-weakening of quoted-delimiter opacity, all 4 fixture cells) -- faithful match, no drift or scope narrowing. One non-blocking note: ${ has no dedicated real-shell repro cell (unlike $( and backtick), a fail-closed defense-in-depth choice under R1 rather than a proven-exploit cell -- recommended as a nice-to-have 5th regression cell for QA, not a gate. Phase 2.5 does not re-run (design.json/sketches stand, additive-only per BA's and the judge's own synthesis); proceeding directly to Phase 3.

QA-first (3a/3b). 3a: QA authored 12-AC failing contract at dcc9b4b (671 passed/13 failed pre-implementation, all correctly targeted). 3b: Dev implemented design.json's Sketch A (heredoc bodies as a 4th opaque region, delimiter capture reusing existing quote-aware word-building machinery, AC12's coarse deny-on-sighting guard for unquoted $(/backtick/${). Found and fixed 2 real bugs along the way: a dead-fast-path skip that never captured non-git heredoc delimiters, and a quadratic-cost regression in the body-skip walk (measured 292ms->8833ms at 3072B->65536B, fixed to linear 292ms->884ms). qa_signoff.verdict=APPROVE, no scope drift. PR #144 opened. Local checks green across every suite referencing pre-tool-use.sh, modulo 2 pre-existing/unrelated rows confirmed via git-stash-against-baseline (corpus-drift AC4, and AC12's own explicitly-non-required 5th EXTRA cell, structurally unreachable given an unrelated pre-existing *git* prefilter). Pre-Phase-4 gate initially FAILED (impl-report.json requirement_checks[8] missing required 'notes' field, the AC12-EXTRA SKIP entry which only had 'justification'); orchestrator fixed directly (added notes summarizing the existing justification, a metadata-only fix, no design/implementation judgment involved) and re-ran the gate clean. Frontend gate: SKIP (no frontend surface). Mis-tier tripwire and live-verification gate: not applicable (architectural tier already; no data migration). Separately confirmed: main's own CI (tests.yml) has been failing on every commit since before this issue's own first checkpoint (9d070bf, pre-dating this whole run), root-caused to the same known, deliberately-deferred corpus-drift tripwire -- not caused by #138 or #140's own changes.

Round 1, dispatched via Workflow tool (6 agents, reviewed HEAD 31ba3e8). BA APPROVE (spec-intent match, no scope drift, AC12-EXTRA SKIP correctly disclosed). DevOps APPROVE (confirmed no infra/CI surface, independent of round-3 Phase 2 finding). Dev APPROVE (independently re-verified both of Dev's own self-reported bugfixes -- the dead-fast-path capture bug and the quadratic-cost regression -- with fresh reproductions, both confirmed real and correctly fixed). DBA APPROVE_WITH_NOTES: 1 major, NOT blocking -- AC12's coarse deny is spec-conformant but causes real, unrecorded false-positive denials on legitimate git workflows (e.g. writing release notes with an unquoted ${VERSION} heredoc then narrowly staging that file), reproduced live against both refs; asks for the cost to be written into design.json residual_risks or a follow-up issue before merge. QA REQUEST_CHANGES: (1) confirms and extends DBA's finding with more firing cases (git status --porcelain with no staging at all, narrow git commit -m <path>), frames it as a genuine SPEC CONTRADICTION between AC12 (coarse deny) and R8/AC5/AC10 (narrow-stage-after-body must allow) for BA to rule on, not a Dev defect; (2) mutation-proved the ${ entry of AC12's rule table is DEAD -- dropping the ${ pattern from both check sites leaves the suite byte-identical green (682/2), zero live coverage despite AC12 requiring it; (3) AC12 EXTRA's SKIP justification is factually true but leaves a permanently-red row normalizing suite failure, one-line fix available (add a git mention to the fixture) and previously proposed by Dev itself but not applied; (4) a comment claims a regression-budget re-measurement on a many-blank-line corpus that does not exist -- QA took the real measurement, the named cost did not materialize, comment should be struck; (5)/(6) stale README figures and branch 4 commits behind main, rebase needed before merge (QA checked the one way it could matter -- #138's only hooks.json change -- and confirmed it does not invalidate anything measured here). SecOps VETO, the dispositive finding: independently re-derived and confirmed AC12's 4 required cells hold, and swept 701 consecutive byte-offsets across the two/three-char trigger with 0 escapes -- the Phase 2.5 VETO's own subject is genuinely closed. But found a NEW, serious, unrelated-to-AC12 defect: _hd_skip's exit condition (_hdtoolong, pre-tool-use.sh:999) is set whenever a heredoc body LINE merely straddles the scanner's internal refill/window boundary, not only when it genuinely exceeds a whole window as the code's own comment claims -- and when set, the terminator comparison for that line is suppressed, so opacity silently runs to end of command and everything after (a trailing git add -A) is never scanned: an ALLOW. Measured on a completely ordinary 1042-byte cat <<-EOF command (6 prose lines + padding + git add -A, no adversarial quote/expansion tricks at all): gate allows it; real bash/zsh/sh via a recording-git-shim all confirm git genuinely runs. Reproduced across a length-swept grid: exposure 0.52% (naive line-length x line-count grid) up to 24% (consecutive pad lengths on the <<- + prose shape) -- not a rare corner case. Mutation-proved that NONE of the 12 ACs constrain this term: reverting _hdtoolong=1 to =0 passes all 25 re-derived AC1-AC12 rows while changing live-input behavior. SecOps specified the correct-fix property (gate verdict must equal a real-shell-oracle observation swept across >=1100 consecutive body lengths spanning >=2 full internal window periods, both halves: recognize a genuine terminator regardless of window alignment, AND never mistake a body-line fragment for the terminator) rather than prescribing a mechanism. Two additional non-blocking findings from SecOps: the same AC12-EXTRA red row QA flagged (medium, needs a filed issue or a fix, not left silently deferred only in impl-report.json), and confirmation that ${ has zero live suite coverage (matching QA-2). peer-review.json merged; shards synced back to $PIPELINE_BASE/140. Per the standard Phase-4-VETO loop-back, NOT returning to Phase 1 wholesale: dispatching BA (narrow ruling on the AC12-vs-R8/AC5/AC10 spec tension DBA/QA both raised) and the Phase 2.5 JUDGE (ruling on SecOps's VETO -- the refill-boundary bug reads as a Dev implementation defect in the shared internal-window primitive, not a distinguishing feature of either sketch's stance, so the judge's ruling is expected but not assumed) in parallel; sketches are NOT re-run.

Judge: Sketch A stands. Both sketches' body-walk functions run on the file's refilled scanner windows, and neither sketch's design-level text prescribed how to distinguish a line that genuinely exceeds a window from one that merely straddles a refill boundary -- that is a byte-level coding decision, not a design-level one. Sketch B's actual novelty was entirely in delimiter capture (the duplication risk that was the deciding factor against it), not terminator detection. Ruled the refill-boundary bug orthogonal to the sketch choice. Wrote a 6th design.json residual_risks entry with the required fix property verbatim from SecOps: gate verdict must equal a real-shell-oracle sweep across >=1100 consecutive body lengths spanning >=2 full window periods; both halves (recognize a genuine terminator regardless of window alignment, AND never mistake a body-line fragment for the terminator); plus a required gate-bites proof (plant unconditional _hdtoolong=1, watch the new sweep fail; revert, watch it pass). BA: AC12 split, not accepted or narrowed wholesale. ${ (bare parameter expansion) NARROWED OUT of the coarse trigger entirely -- verified live that bare ${...} cannot itself execute a command, and any $(/backtick nested inside ${...} is still independently caught by the unmodified raw-text scan. Backtick ACCEPTED as a deliberate tradeoff, NOT narrowed -- backtick is not a structural character in _STRUCT at all (unlike '(', which lets $( safely hand back to ordinary top-level scanning); narrowing it would need real tokenization, which SecOps's round-3 VETO explicitly rejected as more than the minimum. Tracked as new follow-up issue #145. Resolved the R8/AC5/AC10-vs-AC12 framing as not an unresolved contradiction: R8 governs the pre-existing no-$(/backtick fixture population, AC12 is a deliberate narrower override for bodies that DO contain $(/backtick. spec.json AC12 rewritten (3 new fixture cells), falsifiability_pass updated, ba_notes appended. Side effect: this narrowing MOOTS QA's dead-${-mutation panel finding -- no ${ check remains in the trigger for a mutation to kill. Proceeding to a Phase 3 QA-first re-round (3a rework of the existing contract, not fresh authorship) covering: SecOps's refill-boundary sweep property, BA's revised AC12 fixture cells (including retiring/revising the now-stale AC12-EXTRA bare-${ row), QA's other panel findings (strike the unsubstantiated blank-line regression-budget comment, stale README figures), and a rebase onto current main (branch was 4 commits behind at panel time).

Delta round (DBA + SecOps + QA only, reviewed HEAD 6f13ea2). SecOps APPROVE_WITH_NOTES: round-1 VETO independently re-derived as genuinely closed (1201/1201 sweep vs 536/601 allow at the pre-fix ref; mutation battery with a declared, structurally-justified survivor; zero regressions across 1050+ paired cells; fix is even faster than before). Own low-severity note: found the SAME general mechanism DBA/QA escalate below (a same-line quote after $( defeats detection) but scored it non-blocking because that exact minimal repro is at parity with origin/main (both none), so not a regression by SecOps's framing. DBA REQUEST_CHANGES (1 blocker): round-1 major genuinely resolved (${ narrowing verified, backtick tradeoff properly discharged via issue #145, self-filed and verified). But found, independently of QA, that AC12's $( hand-back (required for AC12(b)'s narrow-vs-blanket discrimination) returns without consuming _sc, so ordinary top-level scanning resumes over the raw heredoc body -- re-entering the exact quote-parity regime #140 exists to close. 53-byte repro: unquoted heredoc body containing $(echo hi) followed by an odd single quote on the same or a later line, then a real terminator and a trailing git add -A, denies nowhere -- confirmed via gate driver and a real-shell oracle across bash/zsh/sh. Regression control shows this is NOT a regression (removing the $( makes the plain case correctly deny; the fix does close everything except this specific combination) -- an unclosed sub-case, not a newly-introduced one. Specified the required property: the full 27-cell cross product of {odd-single, odd-double, balanced} x {$(, backtick, neither} x {blanket, narrow, no command} must equal a shim-oracle observation. QA REQUEST_CHANGES: independently found and reproduced the SAME class of gap (QA-R2-1, high) with a more minimal same-line repro, confirmed not a regression (pre=none/post=none on all 8 tested cells), confirmed live-input-reachable and disclosed nowhere (not spec.json, not design.json residual_risks, not issue #145). Consequential finding: #145's own proposed remedy (give backtick a $(-style hand-back recognizer) would IMPORT this exact hole into the one arm currently immune -- #145 needs correcting before anyone implements it as currently written. QA-R2-2 (medium): the backtick over-denial tradeoff BA accepted has no pinning assertion in either direction, violating this file's own stated 'both halves of one trade-off, or neither' discipline -- a future change could silently narrow or widen it with nothing going red. QA-R2-3/4 (low): AC7 SUPPLEMENT measures a path blank lines inside a heredoc never actually reach (still no regression found at the right path, re-measured, same conclusion); spec.json AC12 still carries a literal '#<TBD-follow-up>' placeholder instead of citing #145. All 6 round-1 findings re-verified independently rather than trusted: QA-1 half-resolved/half-properly-deferred, QA-2 resolved (moot), QA-3 resolved (deleted not relabeled), QA-5 genuinely not resolved (README still stale, not in this diff), QA-6 resolved (rebased, confirmed via merge-base ancestor check). QA's own full suite run: 1802 passed/1 failed (the same known AC4 corpus-drift, confirmed via git-ls-tree at both refs). Peer-review shards merged; DBA and QA both explicit that this is NOT asking for a Dev code fix necessarily -- QA states plainly it is not asking Dev to close QA-R2-1 in code, only for a ruling on whether it is an accepted, disclosed gap (#118-class) or must close, either way pinned with real assertions. Routing one more scoped BA ruling before any further Dev/QA round.

flags.summary: Dev fix round complete (d36f625, PR #144 force-pushed with lease after the earlier rebase). Root cause of SecOps's VETO: _hd_skip's _hdtoolong flag conflated 'line not yet fully buffered' with 'line genuinely too long', so a terminator line straddling the scanner's internal refill boundary had its comparison suppressed, letting opacity run to end-of-command. Fixed by replacing it with incremental _hdcand/_hdmismatch prefix matching (grows one refill chunk at a time, locks on first mismatch). Gate-bites proof done properly: planted the exact unconditional-mismatch mutation, confirmed the AC13 sweep reddened, reverted via git checkout (not hand-edit), confirmed green again. AC12 narrowed per BA's ruling (bare ${ dropped from the trigger, $(  and backtick unchanged). Full suite: test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh 1802/1 (1 = known AC4 drift); all other suites clean except test-pretooluse-timeout-bound.sh at 122/2, where Dev correctly diagnosed (but did not touch, per QA-ownership discipline) a stale hardcoded 4/4 timing-guard count that QA's own necessary AC7 SUPPLEMENT block pushed to 5/5. Orchestrator fixed that one-line literal directly (6f13ea2, mechanical, verified true count via awk before editing), re-ran the suite: 123/1, confirmed the sole remaining failure is the same known AC4 drift. Pre-Phase-4 gate re-run clean. Dispatching a DELTA Phase 4 round (DBA + SecOps + QA only -- the three non-APPROVE roles; BA/DevOps/Dev's clean APPROVEs are unaffected by a security-scanner bugfix and its test coverage, nothing in their domains changed).

QA reworked the failing-test contract (b6f57a0, rebased onto 8fb0e17) per the Phase-4 VETO + BA's AC12 ruling: new AC13 refill-boundary sweep (1100 consecutive body lengths, real-shell oracle + near-miss negative control), AC12 cells revised for the dropped bare-${ trigger, AC12-EXTRA retired, AC7 blank-line claim backed with a real measurement (a real bug in QA's own harness -- $() stripping trailing newlines -- found and fixed along the way). 1038 legitimate new red rows (1035 from the sweep confirming SecOps's bug, 3 from AC12's ${ narrowing not yet implemented) + 1 pre-existing unrelated (AC4). Dispatching Dev for Phase 3b next.

QA authored Phase 3a failing-test contract (12 ACs) at dcc9b4b in worktree .claude/worktrees/140-phase3-20260903-162931, branch fix/140-heredoc-opacity. 671 passed/13 failed pre-implementation: 12 legitimate new-contract failures (11 #140 AC rows + 1 bonus AC7 density-axis exposure from reverting dens_pad's padding), 1 pre-existing unrelated corpus-drift AC4 failure. Dispatching Dev for Phase 3b next.
